headline: High Arctic Expedition Planning and Permits
reservation: Travelers must register with Parks Canada in Resolute Bay before entering the park for safety and conservation monitoring. There are no developed facilities or campgrounds; all visitors must be self-sufficient for wilderness travel. A compulsory orientation session regarding polar bear safety and cultural sites is required upon arrival in the gateway community.

days.title: Resolute Bay Orientation

stops.name: Parks Canada Office Resolute
stops.detail: Complete mandatory registration and receive the latest ice and weather briefings for Bathurst Island.

stops.name: Qloqut Point
stops.detail: Explore the outskirts of the community to observe High Arctic flora and archaeological remains before heading to the park.

days.driving: Local walking or ATV transfer; logistics are entirely weather-dependent.
days.note: Aircraft charters to the park are subject to sudden delays due to fog or wind.

days.title: Bathurst Island Wilderness
days.start: Suggested: 8 AM via Twin Otter Charter

stops.name: May Inlet
stops.detail: Witness the stark beauty of the High Arctic landscape, characterized by rolling hills and polar desert terrain.

stops.name: Peary Caribou Habitat
stops.detail: Observe the critical calving grounds for the endangered Peary Caribou from a respectful distance.

days.driving: No roads; travel is via air charter or arduous trekking; conditions vary.
days.note: Total self-reliance is required; there are no marked trails or emergency shelters in the park.

days.title: Arctic Marine Ecology

stops.name: Goodsir Inlet
stops.detail: Explore the coastal margins where marine mammals such as walrus or seals may be spotted near the ice edge.

stops.name: Polar Desert Plateau
stops.detail: Hike the interior barren lands to see unique geological formations and hardy arctic wildflowers.

days.driving: Trekking only; terrain is uneven and saturated during the summer melt.
days.note: Polar bear monitors or high-level predator awareness are essential for any coastal activity.

intel.title: Aircraft Staging
intel.text: There is no vehicle parking; logistics are managed through the Resolute Bay Airport tarmac. Equipment is staged at the airport or local expediting warehouses.

intel.title: Remote Communication
intel.text: No cellular or radio towers exist within the park. Visitors must carry a satellite phone and an emergency beacon (PLB) at all times.

intel.title: Resolute Supply
intel.text: All fuel for stoves or heaters must be purchased and flown in from Resolute Bay. There are no resources available once you depart the gateway town.

intel.title: Short Summer Window
intel.text: The park is generally only accessible in July and August when the snow has cleared sufficiently for Twin Otter landings on the tundra. High winds can occur at any time.

intel.title: Charter Logistics
intel.text: Access is almost exclusively by chartered aircraft from Resolute Bay. These flights are expensive and require coordination months in advance with local airlines.

plan.arrival: Fly into Resolute Bay via scheduled commercial service from Iqaluit or Ottawa; meet with your expedition expeditor for gear check.
plan.vehicle: No road vehicles are used; travel within the park is strictly by foot or specialized aircraft landing on unprepared strips.
plan.goldenHour: Resolute Bay Coastline, where the low-angled sun illuminates the pack ice during the brief summer season.
